title: The city of the future
paragraphs: For centuries, people have moved to and lived in cities. These sprawling urban centres are places to find work, friends and fun. It's no surprise that they continue to grow as more and more people flood in hoping to make the most of the opportunities they offer but adding to the congestion and pollution that already exists.

According to a report by the United Nations, 54 per cent of the world's population lives in urban areas and it predicts that by 2050, this figure will have increased to around 70 per cent. But as more and more people migrate from the countryside to the city to get better opportunities, they can end up with nowhere to live.

This is true in places such as Rio de Janeiro, where migrants can't rent or buy a home, and they end up building their own communities and houses on unoccupied land. These are called shanty towns - poor communities where the houses are built out of cheap materials like corrugated iron and plastic sheeting — and often don't have any electricity or water supply.

These are, of course, not the megacities of the future we want to see. Some serious urban planning is needed to make our cities of the future good, safe and modern places to live in. This involves improving the infrastructure, the housing conditions and also the opportunities for education and employment.

Something urban planners are looking at now is the creation of 'smart cities'. According to John Rossant, founder and chairman of the non-profit organisation New Cities Foundation, technology is the way forward. He thinks that it's generally accepted that "cloud computing, ubiquitous internet, robust 5G networks etc, will transform our cities." He says technology is really "a game changer", in urbanisation. It would collect large amounts of data about how a city is performing and may improve how a city functions.

This may sound like a utopian view. For now, some cities and conurbations around the world are trying out more low-tech schemes to try and make them desirable places to live and work in. Building shared-ownership housing and improving public transport are some ways. And encouraging cycling and building bike lanes can keep the population healthy and cut down on smog. What would make your city a better place to live in?

vocabulary.entry: sprawling [adj.] /ˈsprɔːlɪŋ/ 蔓延的；杂乱无序伸展的
vocabulary.example: The sprawling city extends for miles.
vocabulary.translation: 这座不断扩展的城市绵延数英里。

vocabulary.entry: urban [adj.] /ˈɜːbən/ 城市的；都市的
vocabulary.example: Urban areas are often more crowded than rural ones.
vocabulary.translation: 城市地区通常比农村更拥挤。

vocabulary.entry: flood in [phr.] /flʌd ɪn/ 涌入；大量进入 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: Applications flooded in after the job was advertised.
vocabulary.translation: 招聘广告发布后，求职申请大量涌入。

vocabulary.entry: make the most of [phr.] /meɪk ðə məʊst əv/ 充分利用 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: We should make the most of our time.
vocabulary.translation: 我们应该充分利用我们的时间。

vocabulary.entry: congestion [n.] /kənˈdʒestʃən/ 拥堵；拥挤
vocabulary.example: Traffic congestion is a major problem in big cities.
vocabulary.translation: 交通拥堵是大城市的主要问题。

vocabulary.entry: migrate [v.] /maɪˈɡreɪt/ 迁移；移居
vocabulary.example: Many people migrate to cities for work.
vocabulary.translation: 许多人为了工作迁移到城市。

vocabulary.entry: shanty town [n.] /ˈʃænti taʊn/ 棚户区；贫民窟
vocabulary.example: Shanty towns have poor living conditions.
vocabulary.translation: 棚户区的生活条件很差。

vocabulary.entry: corrugated iron [n.] /ˈkɒrəɡeɪtɪd ˈaɪən/ 波纹铁皮
vocabulary.example: The roof is made of corrugated iron.
vocabulary.translation: 屋顶是用波纹铁皮做的。

vocabulary.entry: plastic sheeting [n.] /ˈplæstɪk ˈʃiːtɪŋ/ 塑料布
vocabulary.example: They covered the building site with plastic sheeting.
vocabulary.translation: 他们用塑料布覆盖了建筑工地。

vocabulary.entry: megacity [n.] /ˈmeɡəsɪti/ 特大城市
vocabulary.example: Tokyo is a megacity with over 30 million people.
vocabulary.translation: 东京是一个拥有超过3000万人口的特大城市。

vocabulary.entry: infrastructure [n.] /ˈɪnfrəstrʌktʃə/ 基础设施
vocabulary.example: The government is investing in transport infrastructure.
vocabulary.translation: 政府正在投资交通基础设施。

vocabulary.entry: smart city [n.] /smɑːt ˈsɪti/ 智慧城市 (专业词汇)
vocabulary.example: Smart cities use technology to improve services.
vocabulary.translation: 智慧城市利用技术改善服务。

vocabulary.entry: ubiquitous [adj.] /juːˈbɪkwɪtəs/ 无处不在的 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: Smartphones have become ubiquitous in daily life.
vocabulary.translation: 智能手机在日常生活中已经无处不在。

vocabulary.entry: robust [adj.] /rəʊˈbʌst/ 强健的；强劲的
vocabulary.example: The economy is showing robust growth.
vocabulary.translation: 经济呈现出强劲的增长态势。

vocabulary.entry: game changer [n.] /ˈɡeɪm tʃeɪndʒə/ 改变游戏规则的事物 (口语；固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: This invention is a real game changer.
vocabulary.translation: 这项发明是一个真正的变革因素。

vocabulary.entry: utopian [adj.] /juːˈtəʊpiən/ 乌托邦的；空想的
vocabulary.example: His plan sounds utopian and unrealistic.
vocabulary.translation: 他的计划听起来空想且不现实。

vocabulary.entry: conurbation [n.] /ˌkɒnəˈbeɪʃən/ 组合城市；城市群 (地理学词汇)
vocabulary.example: The Manchester conurbation is densely populated.
vocabulary.translation: 曼彻斯特城市群人口密集。

vocabulary.entry: shared-ownership housing [n.] /ʃeəd ˈəʊnəʃɪp ˈhaʊzɪŋ/ 共有产权住房 (专业词汇)
vocabulary.example: Shared-ownership housing helps first-time buyers.
vocabulary.translation: 共有产权住房帮助首次购房者。

vocabulary.entry: bike lane [n.] /baɪk leɪn/ 自行车道
vocabulary.example: The city is building more bike lanes.
vocabulary.translation: 这座城市正在修建更多的自行车道。

vocabulary.entry: cut down on [phr.] /kʌt daʊn ɒn/ 减少；削减 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: You should cut down on sugar.
vocabulary.translation: 你应该减少糖的摄入。

vocabulary.entry: unoccupied [adj.] /ʌnˈɒkjupaɪd/ 空闲的；未被占用的
vocabulary.example: The house has been unoccupied for years.
vocabulary.translation: 这所房子已经空置多年了。

vocabulary.entry: urbanisation [n.] /ˌɜːbənaɪˈzeɪʃən/ 城市化 (英式拼写，美式: urbanization)
vocabulary.example: Urbanisation has increased rapidly in developing countries.
vocabulary.translation: 发展中国家的城市化迅速加快。

vocabulary.entry: desirable [adj.] /dɪˈzaɪərəbəl/ 理想的；值得拥有的
vocabulary.example: This is a desirable location for a new school.
vocabulary.translation: 这是新学校的理想位置。

vocabulary.entry: smog [n.] /smɒɡ/ 雾霾
vocabulary.example: Smog is a serious health hazard in many cities.
vocabulary.translation: 雾霾是许多城市严重的健康危害。

sentences.english: For centuries, people have moved to and lived in cities.
sentences.chinese: 几个世纪以来，人们不断迁移并居住在城市里。

sentences.english: These sprawling urban centres are places to find work, friends and fun.
sentences.chinese: 这些不断扩展的城市中心是人们寻找工作、结交朋友和享受乐趣的地方。

sentences.english: It's no surprise that they continue to grow as more and more people flood in hoping to make the most of the opportunities they offer but adding to the congestion and pollution that already exists.
sentences.chinese: 毫不奇怪，随着越来越多的人涌入城市，希望充分利用城市提供的各种机会，城市还在持续发展壮大，但这也加剧了已经存在的拥堵和污染问题。

sentences.english: According to a report by the United Nations, 54 per cent of the world's population lives in urban areas and it predicts that by 2050, this figure will have increased to around 70 per cent.
sentences.chinese: 根据联合国的一份报告，全球54%的人口居住在城市地区，并且该报告预测，到2050年，这一比例将上升到大约70%。

sentences.english: But as more and more people migrate from the countryside to the city to get better opportunities, they can end up with nowhere to live.
sentences.chinese: 但是，随着越来越多的人从农村迁移到城市以获取更好的机会，他们最终将没有地方来生存。

sentences.english: This is true in places such as Rio de Janeiro, where migrants can't rent or buy a home, and they end up building their own communities and houses on unoccupied land.
sentences.chinese: 在诸如里约热内卢这样的地方就是如此，移民们租不起也买不起房子，于是他们最终在闲置的土地上建造起自己的社区和房屋。

sentences.english: These are called shanty towns - poor communities where the houses are built out of cheap materials like corrugated iron and plastic sheeting — and often don't have any electricity or water supply.
sentences.chinese: 这些地方被称为棚户区——贫困社区，那里的房屋是用波纹铁皮和塑料布等廉价材料建造的——而且通常没有电和水供应。

sentences.english: These are, of course, not the megacities of the future we want to see.
sentences.chinese: 当然，这些并不是我们希望看到的未来的特大城市的样子。

sentences.english: Some serious urban planning is needed to make our cities of the future good, safe and modern places to live in.
sentences.chinese: 需要进行一些严肃的城市规划，以使我们未来的城市成为良好、安全且现代化的宜居之地。

sentences.english: This involves improving the infrastructure, the housing conditions and also the opportunities for education and employment.
sentences.chinese: 这包括改善基础设施、住房条件，以及增加教育和就业机会。

sentences.english: Something urban planners are looking at now is the creation of 'smart cities'.
sentences.chinese: 城市规划者们目前正在关注的一件事是“智慧城市”的创建。

sentences.english: According to John Rossant, founder and chairman of the non-profit organisation New Cities Foundation, technology is the way forward.
sentences.chinese: 据非营利组织新城市基金会的创始人兼主席约翰·罗桑特称，科技是未来的发展方向。

sentences.english: He thinks that it's generally accepted that "cloud computing, ubiquitous internet, robust 5G networks etc, will transform our cities."
sentences.chinese: 他认为，“云计算、无处不在的互联网、强大的5G网络等等，将改变我们的城市”这一观点已被普遍接受。

sentences.english: He says technology is really "a game changer", in urbanisation.
sentences.chinese: 他说，在城市化进程中，科技确实是“改变游戏规则的因素”。

sentences.english: It would collect large amounts of data about how a city is performing and may improve how a city functions.
sentences.chinese: 它将收集大量有关城市运行情况的数据，并有可能改善城市运行的方式。

sentences.english: This may sound like a utopian view.
sentences.chinese: 这听起来可能像是一种乌托邦式的观点。

sentences.english: For now, some cities and conurbations around the world are trying out more low-tech schemes to try and make them desirable places to live and work in.
sentences.chinese: 目前，世界上一些城市和城市群正在尝试更多的低技术方案，试图使它们成为理想的生活和工作场所。

sentences.english: Building shared-ownership housing and improving public transport are some ways.
sentences.chinese: 建设共有产权住房和改善公共交通就是一些方法。

sentences.english: And encouraging cycling and building bike lanes can keep the population healthy and cut down on smog.
sentences.chinese: 而且鼓励骑自行车和修建自行车道可以让人们保持健康，同时减少雾霾。

sentences.english: What would make your city a better place to live in?
sentences.chinese: 你认为怎么做能让你的城市成为一个更宜居的地方呢？
